Notice of Annual General Meeting
Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that it will hold its Annual General Meeting ("AGM") at the offices of Haynes Boone, Alder Castle, 10 Noble Street, London EC2V 7JX on 24 September 2026 at 12:00 noon. The full Notice of Annual General Meeting (the "Notice") will be available on the Company's website
www.kropz.com
and is being posted to shareholders today, together with a Form of Proxy.
It should, however, be noted that completion of the audit of the Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 (the "2026 Accounts") is currently in progress and it has not been possible to publish these prior to the issue of this Notice. Therefore no resolution to receive and adopt the 2026 Accounts is being proposed at the AGM.
The Company expects to publish its 2026 Accounts by no later than 30 September 2026. Following the publication of the 2026 Accounts, a separate general meeting will be held later in the year at which such a resolution will be proposed.

New Loan FacilityandOperational Update
Kropz Plc (AIM: KRPZ), an emerging African phosphate producer and developer, announces that Kropz Elandsfontein (Pty) Ltd ("
Elandsfontein
")
and Ubunto-Botho Investments (Pty) Ltd
("
UBI
")
(together the "
Parties
") have agreed to a ZAR 200 million (approximately US$ 12.3 million) (the "
Loan
"), which constitutes a related party transaction.
Operational Update
The Elandsfontein mine continues to progress through its production ramp-up phase. As previously announced, record monthly production was achieved in March with over 40,000 tonnes of production. However, mining operations continue to be materially affected by variability in the ore body, including the nature and volume of slimes material, hard bank and pink ore encountered within the deposit. These conditions have resulted in slower mining rates and lower concentrate output in the quarter ended 30 June 2026. Production was also disrupted in the quarter due to availability of the mining contractor, which interrupted ore flow to the processing plant and constrained the operational flexibility required to sustain more stable production levels.
Geopolitical tensions have created additional commercial headwinds with higher energy and consumable costs, and an increase in freight rates.
Elandsfontein produced 95 956 tonnes of phosphate concentrate in quarter ended 30 June 2026 (115,686: quarter to 31 March 2026) representing a 17% decrease compared quarter to quarter. Sales for the period totalled 183,714 tonnes, and stock at the quarter end was higher than anticipated being approximately 94,000 tonnes.
The operational issues, combined with the market factors described above, has given rise to a further working capital funding requirement. Consequently, the Company has entered into the Loan with UBI to support the group.
The Loan will be used by Elandsfontein to fund its cashflow and operational expenditure needs.
The Loan
Elandsfontein and UBI have agreed terms for a loan facility of ZAR 200 million (approximately US$ 12.3 million). Interest is payable on the Loan at the South African prime overdraft interest rate plus 6%, nominal per annum and compounded monthly. The Loan is repayable on the earlier of a date as agreed between the Parties or on demand from UBI, on no less than 15 business days' notice. There is no fixed term.
As announced on 21 May 2025 and 28 May 2025, Kropz SA (Pty) Ltd has issued a Guarantee, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of the ARC Fund (
ARC
), and Kropz Plc has issued a Limited Indemnity, Security Cession and Pledge in favour of ARC for all current and future loan facilities made to Elandsfontein, which are applicable to the Loan.These agreements will be extended by the parties in favour of UBI as the first ranking priority (through an Omnibus agreement), and ARC and the second ranking priority issued by Kropz SA (Pty) Ltd for all current and future loan facilities of Kropz Elandsfontein.
The Company will update the market on drawdown of the Loan in due course.
Related Party Transaction
UBI is the indirect controlling shareholder of ARC, and consequently the Loan and the Omnibus agreement are related party transactions pursuant to Rule 13 of the AIM Rules for Companies. Gerrit Duminy, a director of the Company, is the representative of ARC. Accordingly, Gerrit Duminy has not been involved in the approval of the Loan by the Company's board. The directors of the Company, who are considered independent for the purposes of the Loan, having consulted with the Company's nominated adviser, consider the terms of the Loan to be fair and reasonable insofar as the Company's shareholders are concerned.

company_30s.what_they_do: KRPZ is a resource exploration firm that focuses on developing the Hinda copper project in the Republic of Congo. The company’s core activities involve drilling, resource estimation, and securing permits to move the site from exploration into production.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Copper demand is rising as the world pushes toward electric vehicles and renewable energy. The Hinda project sits on a large copper‑bearing zone that could supply a significant portion of the global market if it reaches commercial scale. KRPZ’s presence in Congo gives it access to a low‑cost resource base and a strategic location for downstream buyers.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the development phase, relying heavily on loan facilities and equity raises to fund drilling and permitting. Cash burn is high and revenue is non‑existent, but recent funding rounds and a new loan facility suggest the company is actively working to stay solvent and push the project forward.

rns_narrative: KRPZ has been busy securing financing and managing its debt structure. Over the past year, the company has announced a bridge loan drawdown, a new loan facility, and a WRAP retail offer to raise capital. Governance changes—such as a new nominated adviser and an upcoming AGM—highlight the firm’s focus on keeping the board and shareholders aligned.

Operationally, the company is progressing on the Hinda site, with a recent ECA approval and admission of shares that signal regulatory compliance. The AGM will provide an opportunity for shareholders to review the project’s status and vote on key decisions.

The narrative shows a company that is adapting to funding constraints while keeping its flagship project on track. The recent announcements suggest a pivot toward securing the capital needed to move from exploration to the next phase of development.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silent optimism around the Hinda copper project
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls see the Hinda project as a hidden gem; they believe the company’s focus on copper and its strategic location could unlock substantial upside if the project reaches commercial scale.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that heavy debt, a lack of revenue, and the risk of delisting could crush the firm. They point to the repeated loan facilities and the fact that the company has not yet generated cash flow.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community has moved from neutral to quietly bullish as new funding news and operational updates surface, but overall chatter remains thin.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat, meaning there is no public hype. A sudden news event could therefore generate a surprise rebound.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM on 1 Sep 2026 will allow shareholders to approve the latest loan terms and potentially authorize further capital raises.
A successful drilling result at Hinda could trigger a positive market reaction and attract institutional interest.
Any announcement that the company has secured a long‑term off‑take agreement or a joint venture would act as a strong catalyst.
If commodity prices for copper climb above the company’s break‑even threshold, it could improve the project’s economics and boost investor confidence.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that breaks the 52‑week low, a clear announcement of additional funding, or a positive drilling report. A move above the key support level around the 52‑week low would be a strong confirmation of mean reversion.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a recovery cycle—capitulation may be complete, but the accumulation of smart money is still weak. The APEX score indicates a tight compression, so a breakout could come soon if the catalyst materialises.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company sits on a deep‑crashed asset with a high upside if the Hinda project moves forward. A 70‑95% drop creates a steep reward curve: if the share price recovers to roughly half of its 52‑week high, the upside could be 2‑3× the current value. The historical performance of similar deep‑crash signals shows that a 50‑60% rebound is not uncommon after a catalyst.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the company fails to secure sufficient funding or that the Hinda project stalls. Without a commercial cash flow, the firm could face another debt restructuring or even delisting. The worst‑case scenario is a further decline to a new, lower trough.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped to the initial investment if a stop is set 20% below the entry. Potential upside is at least 2× the entry price, giving a risk‑to‑reward ratio of 1:2 or better.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a bounce from the 52‑week low, with a 20% stop below that level. Allocate 10% of discretionary capital, scaling in on secondary pullbacks. Monitor volume; a sustained 2‑3× increase in average daily volume is a good sign of accumulation.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the AGM outcome or a positive drilling result. A clear announcement of a new loan or an off‑take agreement would be the trigger to go live.
playbook.if_passing: Only consider exiting if the company files for bankruptcy or is delisted. Otherwise, maintain the position through the recovery.

ai_insights.bottom_line: KRPZ’s deep crash and silent market give a high‑reward contrarian opportunity; if the Hinda project moves forward and a funding catalyst arrives, the upside is substantial while the downside is limited by a tight stop.
